title: Hiding money and equipment left in the car outside the Dew Drop
summary: He never had to hide his pay and bands left equipment in cars at the Dew Drop.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, speaking of money, in those days when you had to, when you got paid, did you ever have to hide your money?

That's one thing you didn't have to worry about, because there wasn't nobody there to, you know, like, see, during those times, the few bad people, who were bad, everybody knew them. And everybody was watching them. So they usually didn't do things where everybody knew them. They would always go to strange places and do things. And so the straight, they just didn't, it just didn't happen. You know, at the Dew Drop, we always talk about this now. You see, we would, the band, all bands would come in from their job. Like I played LSU Baton Rouge from 8 to 12, well, 2 o'clock I'm in New Auburn. Right. We would go straight to the Dew Drop. Find a parking place on LaSalle Street, somewhere around in that era. The top full, the station wagon full, all equipment. Get on out and go on in the Dew Drop. Nobody steal nothing. You do that now. You'd not, or you wouldn't even find a car. But see, this is how much things have changed. And see, this is what got everybody so fearful of things. Man, the first thing I do is when I come in, I want to get my equipment home. When I knock on the first thing I think about, man, look, take my equipment home. Mm-hmm.
